messages:

Subject: Stability escrow: hot-standby + autofallback for FinPay SLA carveout

Hi Maria / FinPay ops team,

Thanks again for the sync this morning. Per our conversation, FinPay is requesting an explicit SLA carveout for the upcoming checkout rollout window (peak US traffic for Q2). To reduce risk while preserving rollout velocity we can offer a "stability escrow": a short-term operational policy that combines three elements:

1) Hot-standby pinned variant — we maintain a pinned, empirically-stable model+runtime variant for your routes that can be instantly routed to in <200ms.
2) Autofallback gating — Canary and A/B traffic will automatically revert to the pinned variant when latency or error budgets breach predefined thresholds.
3) Telemetry escrow & post-mortem SLA credits — we feed detailed token-level latency + error traces to your SREs for the window and commit to crediting service usage if automatic fallback did not trigger appropriately.

We propose the following thresholds for the carveout window (configurable):
- 95th percentile p99 latency for generation endpoints > 650ms (3-minute rolling) -> autofallback to pinned variant
- Error rate (5xx) > 0.6% (5-minute rolling) -> autofallback and page on-call
- If pinned variant capacity is saturated, immediate traffic shedding to a lower-cost global fallback pool (pre-agreed) and notify both teams.

I've attached a one-page stability_escrow_template.pdf that formalizes operational responsibilities. Please confirm whether FinPay can accept these thresholds or share alternate targets and any legal/contract constraints. If you approve, we'll send a DocuSign for the SLA carveout addendum and schedule a deployment-runbook handoff.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

+1 415-555-0192

Hi Naomi — thanks for the note and the template. This approach looks promising and aligns with what our SREs want to see. A couple quick asks before we can sign:

1) Can you provide a short sample of the production telemetry we would get during the escrow window (p99 curves, request volumes, and KV cache hit rates)? A CSV or sample dashboard is fine.
2) For the pinned variant: what is the rollout acceptance test? We need confidence the pinned variant actually matches correctness expectations compared to the canary.
3) Legal flagged the wording around "crediting" — can you clarify how credits are calculated and what the max exposure is for Redwood?

If you can send the telemetry CSV + the DocuSign addendum with clearer credit language, I can fast-track with procurement.

Best,
Maria Jensen
Head of Platform Reliability | FinPay
maria.jensen@finpay.com

Team — looping you in on Maria's asks. Draft answers below; please advise edits before I send telemetry and the DocuSign link.

1) Telemetry sample: I'll attach canary-metrics-20280410.csv containing a 6-hour window (p50/p90/p95/p99 by route, tokens, kv-cache hit rate, batch sizes). Marcus — can you confirm we aren't leaking internal IDs and that retention meets FinPay's policy?

2) Pinned variant acceptance: propose a quick canary acceptance test:
- Comparison set of 200 representative checkout prompts (customer-supplied + our regression set)
- Production-like traffic at 10% traffic load for 30 minutes; automated quality checks (top-level metrics: semantic similarity > 0.92 vs control prompts, no new safety hits).
- If semantic similarity metric drops > 4% vs baseline OR regressions flagged by the regression set, we do not swap — instead we keep the pinned variant and autopin remains until issues are resolved.

3) Credits math: propose cap at 10% of monthly invoice for the affected routes for the escrow window unless there is evidence of operator misconfiguration. Legal can tighten the language, but we should show a sensible exposure cap. Laura — can you draft the addendum paragraph that limits credits to the agreed cap and defines the triggering conditions?

Config snippet (for ops):
- fallback_policy:
  - monitor: p99_latency
  - threshold_ms: 650
  - window: 180s
  - action: route_to: pinned_variant_v3
- pinned_variant_provision: guaranteed_slots: 10

I'll prepare the telemetry CSV and a DocuSign with sample credit wording. Marcus / Aditya, can you review by EOD so I can reply to Maria?

Naomi

Hi Maria — thanks for the quick review. Attached is the telemetry sample you requested (canary-metrics-20280410.csv) and a draft DocuSign addendum that limits credit exposure (see clause 4.2). Key points:

- Telemetry: sample includes p50/p90/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cache hit rates for the main checkout route. No PII present.
- Acceptance: We propose the 200-prompt acceptance test + 30-minute 10% traffic soak; automated regression checks identical to what I outlined earlier.
- Credits: Credit exposure capped at 10% of the monthly invoice for the affected routes for the escrow window. Exceptions for operator misconfig or denial of autoswap are excluded.

Next steps if you approve:
1) Sign DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abcd-ef12-3456
2) Schedule a 30-minute deployment handoff with our SRE (we suggest Apr 18 or 19).
3) We will enable the pinned variant with guaranteed slots and the autofallback policy for the carveout window.

If you want alternative thresholds (tighter p99 or different credit cap), let us know and we'll update the addendum.

Thanks — Naomi
